prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what type of coverage you need (individual/family, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid/CHIP), whether you live on the Missouri or Kansas side of Kansas City, which networks or doctors you want, and whether you prefer in‑person help or virtual support.

If you tell me your ZIP code and what kind of plan you’re shopping for, I can find and shortlist highly rated, licensed brokers near you. In the meantime, here’s how to find a good one and how to evaluate them.

How to find brokers in Kansas City
- Use the Health Insurance Marketplace (HealthCare.gov) if you’re buying an ACA plan — it has local agents/navigators listed.  
- Search “health insurance broker Kansas City” and check Google/ Yelp reviews and BBB ratings.  
- Contact your state insurance department to verify licensing (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance or Kansas Insurance Department).  
- Ask for referrals from friends, family, or your employer.  
- Look for membership in trade groups (National Association of Health Underwriters — local chapters serve KC).

What to look for
- Licensed in your state(s).  
- Experience with the plan type you need (e.g., Medicare specialists for Medicare A/B/Part D).  
- Independent broker vs captive (independent can show multiple carriers; captive represents one company).  
- Clear explanation of fees/commissions and any conflicts of interest.  
- Willingness to help after enrollment (claims and renewal help, annual re‑shopping).  
- Good client references and online reviews.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- How long have you worked with clients in Kansas City and with my type of coverage?  
- Do you represent multiple carriers or one company? Which ones?  
- Do you charge a broker fee or are you paid only by carriers?  
- Can you provide a written plan comparison (premiums, deductibles, out‑of‑pocket max, networks, drug coverage)?  
- Will you help with claims and renewals? How do you handle ongoing support?  
- Can you provide references from local clients?

Red flags
- Refusal to name carriers they work with or to explain fees.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or steer you only to one option without comparisons.  
- Poor reviews about responsiveness or help with claims.

If you want, give me:
- ZIP code, whether you’re in Kansas or Missouri, and
- Type of coverage (individual/family, Medicare, employer plan, Medicaid)
and I’ll compile a short list of highly rated brokers/agents near you and include license verification and reviews.
